title: RDF Support (juneau-rest-server-rdf)

description:
Three new opt-in modules add a themeable, security-hardened admin-console "chrome" (CSS
theme tokens, a status/domain pill component, and FreeMarker-macro composition) on top of
`juneau-rest-server`, without bleeding a template engine or the DataTables toolkit into the
core:

| Module | Adds | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| `juneau-console` | `ConsoleChromeMixin` (dynamic, per-mount-themed `chrome.css` endpoint), `Theme` (`--jc-*` token allowlist grammar), the `chrome.css` / `juneau-console.js` shell assets, the page-contract schema, and `PageContractAssert` (test helper) | `juneau-rest-server`, `juneau-bean-html5` |
| `juneau-console-freemarker` | `ConsoleFreemarkerMixin` (reserved-classpath `base.ftlh` + the `<@tag>` macro, and the `<@console>` / `<@page>` / `<@navigation>` / `<@card>` directives) | `juneau-rest-server-view-freemarker` (`provided`), `juneau-console` |

```xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.apache.juneau</groupId>
    <artifactId>juneau-console</artifactId>
    <version>${juneau.version}</version>
</dependency>
<!-- FreeMarker composition (base.ftlh, <@tag>): -->
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.apache.juneau</groupId>
    <artifactId>juneau-console-freemarker</artifactId>
    <version>${juneau.version}</version>
</dependency>
```

A chrome-only consumer (no FreeMarker, or FreeMarker without DataTables) pulls in exactly one
or two of these — never all three, and never the unrelated `-datatables` module unless it
explicitly asks for the macro.

## Why a security-hardened theme, not a raw CSS override?

Letting a consumer supply arbitrary CSS custom-property values (colors, fonts, a page
background) is an XSS/CSS-injection surface: a naive `var(--jc-page-bg: url(javascript:...))`-
style value sunk into an unescaped stylesheet can exfiltrate data or inject markup. `Theme`
closes that gap with a **normalize-then-accept-known-safe** pipeline, not a denylist:

1. Reject the raw value if it contains any C0/C1/DEL control character (checked *before*
   trimmi...

description:
This is the end-to-end tutorial for adding a page to an admin console built on Juneau: a resource that serves the chrome, a navigation tree, a sortable and searchable table backed by a server-side data endpoint, and a test that pins the page contract. The example is a pet inventory page; substitute your own bean. The reference pages cover each piece in depth. Read them when a step here raises a question. - [Admin-Console Chrome](/docs/topics/AdminConsoleChrome): directives, themes and the page contract. - [Rich Table Views](/docs/topics/RichTableViews): what a table card can do. - [DataTables Server-Side Processing](/docs/topics/DataTables) and [BeanQuery](/docs/topics/JuneauCommonsBeanQuery): the data endpoint. ## What you are building The result looks like the petstore's pets page: the chrome's header and navigation around one table card fed by a server-side data endpoint. ![A finished console page: header, navigation tree and a table card with paging, search and sortable columns](/topics/BuildingAConsolePage.Result.1.png) A console page is four cooperating parts: | Part | Provided by | |---|---| | The chrome template (header, navigation, footer) | `<@console>` and `<@navigation>` in one shared FreeMarker template. | | The page template (its cards) | `<@page>` with one or more `<@card>` elements. | | The data endpoint | A REST operation returning `DataTablesResults`, backed by BeanQuery. | | The assets (CSS, JavaScript) | The mixins `ConsoleChromeMixin`, `ViewsMixin` and `DataTablesMixin`. | `<@page>` is the outermost directive in a page template. description:
A console card can need scripts and stylesheets beyond the `views` toolkit. A datatables card needs jQuery,
DataTables and Juneau's glue script. The card declares that need, and `<@page>` loads each asset once, in
dependency order, after the body has rendered.

## Toolkit packs

A toolkit pack is a named list of CSS and JS assets. A pack can depend on other packs, and it has a kind:

- **VENDOR** packs are libraries and their glue. Their CSS comes before the page `css=`, and their JS comes before
  every runtime script.
- **RUNTIME** packs are Juneau UI runtimes. They keep the position the `views` pack always had.

| Pack | Kind | Loads | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| `jquery` | VENDOR | `jquery.min.js` (WebJar `org.webjars:jquery`) | |
| `datatables` | VENDOR | `dataTables.min.js`, `dataTables.dataTables.min.css` (npm WebJars `datatables.net`, `datatables.net-dt`) | `jquery` |
| `datatables-glue` | VENDOR | `juneau-datatables.js` (served by `DataTablesMixin`) | `datatables` |
| `datatables-buttons` | VENDOR | `dataTables.buttons.min.js`, `buttons.html5.min.js`, `buttons.dataTables.min.css` | `datatables` |
| `views` | RUNTIME | the views runtime | |
| `calendar` | RUNTIME | `juneau-calendar.js`, `juneau-calendar.css` | |
| `xterm` | VENDOR | `xterm.js`, `xterm.css` (npm WebJar `@xterm/xterm`) | |
| `terminal` | RUNTIME | `juneau-terminal.js`, `juneau-terminal.css` (served by `TerminalMixin`) | `views`, `xterm` |
| `charts` | RUNTIME | `juneau-charts.js` (served by `ConsoleChromeMixin`) | |
| `joblog` | RUNTIME | `juneau-joblog.js` (served by `ConsoleChromeMixin`) | |

`datatables-buttons` gives copy and CSV export. Excel and PDF export need JSZip and pdfmake, which aren't
included; register your own pack for them (below).

## What a page loads

`<@page>` loads the packs in `toolkit=`, plus the packs its cards require:

| Card | Requires |
|---|---|
| `type="datatables"` | `datatables-glue`, plus `joblog` when its `detail.region` is a `job-log` region |
| `typ...

description:
A chart card draws a line, bar or donut chart from rows of JSON. Juneau draws it as inline SVG with no third-party
chart library. The script is `juneau-charts.js`, and `<@page>` loads it for you when a page has a chart card.

## A chart from an endpoint

```html
<@card type="chart" id="orders-trend" title="Orders" src="/console/store/stats/daily">
{ kind: 'line', x: { field: 'day', label: 'Day' },
  series: [ { field: 'placed', label: 'Placed' }, { field: 'delivered', label: 'Delivered', tone: 'ok' } ] }
</@card>
```

The endpoint returns an array of flat rows, or an object with a `rows` array:

```json
[ { "day": "Mon", "placed": 3, "delivered": 1 }, { "day": "Tue", "placed": 5, "delivered": 2 } ]
```

From Java, build the same card with `ChartDef`:

```java
page.card(ChartDef.line("orders-trend").title("Orders").src("/console/store/stats/daily")
	.x("day", null, "Day")
	.series("placed", "Placed")
	.series("delivered", "Delivered", "ok")
	.toCardSpec());
```

## Kinds

![A line chart card: orders placed and delivered per day](/topics/ChartCards.Kinds.1.png)

![A bar chart card: pets by status](/topics/ChartCards.Kinds.2.png)

![A donut chart card: pets by species, with the total in the center](/topics/ChartCards.Kinds.3.png)

| Kind | Needs | Options |
|---|---|---|
| `line` | `x`, one or more `series` | `y`, `legend`, `height` |
| `bar` | `x`, one or more `series` | `stacked`, `orientation: 'horizontal'`, `y`, `legend`, `height` |
| `donut` | `label`, `value` | `center` (`'total'` or literal text) |

`x` is a field name, or `{ field, type, label }` where `type` is `category`, `time` or `number`. A series is a
field name, or `{ field, label, tone }`. A tone is `danger`, `ok` or `warning`, or a palette index from 1 to 8; colors come from
the `--jc-chart-1` to `--jc-chart-8` theme properties when a theme sets them.

A donut folds two or more slices under 2% into one "Other" slice.

## Options

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `src=` / `data` | Exactly one. `data` is...

description:
A job-log card starts a long-running job and shows its progress as it runs. It has a small form and a log pane.
Submitting the form posts to your endpoint, which starts an `AsyncJobsMixin` job and returns its `AsyncJobRef`. The
card then streams the job's progress lines and shows the outcome when the job ends. The script is
`juneau-joblog.js`, and `<@page>` loads it for you.

```html
<@card type="job-log" id="rebuild" title="Rebuild index">
{ submit: { endpoint: '/ops/jobs/rebuild', submitLabel: 'Rebuild',
            fields: [ { name: 'shards', label: 'Shards', type: 'number', default: 4 } ] },
  urlParam: 'job' }
</@card>
```

From Java there is no typed builder; use `CardSpec`:

```java
page.card(CardSpec.of("job-log", "rebuild").title("Rebuild index")
	.body("submit", Map.of("endpoint", "/ops/jobs/rebuild", "submitLabel", "Rebuild"))
	.body("urlParam", "job"));
```

## The endpoint

The submit endpoint receives the field values as JSON, plus an `idempotencyKey` that the card mints fresh for every
submit, and returns `AsyncJobRef.of(job)`. Because the card owns that key, a form field named `idempotencyKey` is
rejected when the page renders. Report progress with `job.progress("...")`; each call becomes one line in the log pane,
shown as text. The endpoint may also answer synchronously with an `ActionResult` instead of a job ref; the card then
shows the outcome without a stream. The job's final `ActionResult` sets the banner:

| Outcome | Banner |
|---|---|
| `success` | Done. |
| `failure` | The job failed. |
| `refusal` | The job was refused. |
| `cancelled` | Cancelled. |
| `cancelled-after-effect` | Cancelled after the job had already made changes. |
| `unknown` | The job ended with an unknown outcome. |

The result's `message`, if any, follows the banner text. A `success` banner is styled as ok and every other outcome
as an error.

description: `juneau-console-views` renders data tables and `juneau-console` renders chrome — neither has any concept of a rendered *document*. The optional `juneau-console-views-markdown` module fills that gap: hand it a markdown string, get back an HTML fragment, the same way a `ViewDef` turns a list of beans into a themed table. Because it is a separate, opt-in module, consumers that don't need markdown pay nothing — no markdown parser is dragged into `juneau-rest-server` or the views toolkit by default. ```xml org.apache.juneau juneau-console-views-markdown ${juneau.version} ``` ## The `MarkdownRenderer` SPI The module's single extension point is the library-neutral MarkdownRenderer interface — one method, `String toHtml(String markdown)`, so any parser can sit behind it: ```java MarkdownRenderer renderer = MarkdownRenderer.resolve(); String html = renderer.toHtml("# Runbook\n\nStep one."); ``` `MarkdownRenderer.resolve()` selects the active renderer via the standard `java.util.ServiceLoader` mechanism: - If a consumer registers their own provider (a `META-INF/services/org.apache.juneau.console.views.markdown.MarkdownRenderer` file naming their implementation class), that provider wins. - Otherwise the built-in commonmark-java default is used. description:
`juneau-console-datatables` is an opt-in add-on (not bundled in `juneau-distrib`, the same precedent as
`juneau-rest-server-management-logging`) that wires a [DataTables](https://datatables.net) grid's server-side
processing contract onto [BeanQuery](/docs/topics/JuneauCommonsBeanQuery) — the request/response envelope, the
query-building rules, and a first-party browser glue script. DataTables itself, jQuery, and their CSS remain
**caller-provided**: they are not vendored (their license is not ASF category-A).

```xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.apache.juneau</groupId>
    <artifactId>juneau-console-datatables</artifactId>
    <version>${juneau.version}</version>
</dependency>
```

## The endpoint

A DataTables-backed endpoint takes `@Content DataTablesRequest` and returns `DataTablesResults<T>` (or
`DataTablesResults<List<Object>>` for array rows — see "Array rows" below). `DataTablesMixin` serves the browser
glue script; the resource's own data endpoint is plain `@RestOp`:

```java
@Rest(path="/releases", mixins=DataTablesMixin.class)
public class ReleaseResource extends BasicRestServlet {

    private final InMemoryBeanQueryContext<Release> ctx = InMemoryBeanQueryContext.create(Release.class).build();

    @RestOp(method=POST, path="/query")
    public DataTablesResults<Release> query(@Content DataTablesRequest req) {
        try (var s = ctx.getSession(releases())) {
            return DataTablesQuery.run(req, s);
        }
    }
}
```

:::tip Restrict the endpoint to JSON
Declare `parsers=JsonParser.class` on the data endpoint, e.g. `@RestPost(path="/query", parsers=JsonParser.class)`.
Under `BasicUniversalConfig` a form-urlencoded body would otherwise also bind to `DataTablesRequest`, but
`JuneauDataTables.ajax` only ever sends JSON.
:::

`DataTablesQuery.run(req, session)` builds a `BeanQuery` from the request (via the public
`DataTablesQuery.toBeanQuery(req, ctx)`, usable standalone if you need to inspect or adjust the query before running
it — for exam...

description:
`juneau-console-widgets` is a small, optional module of **declarative widget beans**: plain Java objects that
describe a dialog, a form, a calendar, a row of stat tiles or a badge, plus the first-party browser scripts that paint
them. A bean carries data and a fail-closed `validate()`; it carries no HTML-emitting code. The server-side emitters
live in `juneau-console-views`, which composes these beans, and the dialog/form/bar runtime ships with that module's
`juneau-views.js`.

:::caution Not the same thing as `$W{...}` widgets
Juneau has two unrelated things called "widget":

| | This page | [10.31.2 Widgets](/docs/topics/HtmlWidgets) / [10.31.3 Predefined Widgets](/docs/topics/HtmlPredefinedWidgets) |
|---|---|---|
| Module | `juneau-console-widgets` | `juneau-rest-server` |
| Package | `org.apache.juneau.console.widgets` (plural) | `org.apache.juneau.rest.server.widget` (singular) |
| Core type | `Widget` — a marker interface with `validate()` | `Widget` — an abstract class with `getHtml()` / `getStyle()` / `getScript()` |
| What it is | Typed, data-only beans (modal, form, calendar, badges) | Code that emits raw HTML/CSS/JS into an `@HtmlDocConfig` page via `$W{Name}` |
| Safety model | Typed fields painted with `textContent`; never an HTML sink | Raw markup authored by the application |

The two share nothing but a simple class name, and a `Widget` in your imports is ambiguous if you use both. Import
one by its fully-qualified name.
:::

```xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.apache.juneau</groupId>
    <artifactId>juneau-console-widgets</artifactId>
    <version>${juneau.version}</version>
</dependency>
```

The module depends only on `juneau-rest-server` and `juneau-commons`. It deliberately has **no** dependency on
`juneau-console-views`, so a widget bean can never import a views type.

:::info The runtime lives next to the views module
The script this module ships (`juneau-calendar.js`) resolves its icons through the views
module's `juneau-icon...

description:
`juneau-console-views` is the browser-side toolkit behind the console's table cards: a server-driven table
view with search, sort, paging, a column chooser, saved View Settings, row actions, bulk mutation, cell popovers,
row-detail regions, async-job streaming and shareable links. The server describes a view with plain beans and
annotations; a first-party JavaScript runtime (`juneau-views.js` and its companions) draws it.

![A table card from the petstore: toolbar with paging and search, sortable columns with per-column search, and rows](/topics/RichTableViews.Table.1.png)

Most adopters never touch the view beans directly. You author a `<@card type="datatables">` catalog in a
FreeMarker template (see [Building a Console Page](/docs/topics/BuildingAConsolePage)) and the chrome lifts it into
the view contract for you. This section documents what that catalog can express, the security model behind it, and
the `JuneauViews` JavaScript API for pages that need to go further.

| Page | Covers |
|---|---|
| [Catalog and Columns](/docs/topics/RichTableViewsCatalog) | The datatables catalog, `Column`, search types and operators, `FieldFormat`, `FieldSpan`. |
| [Row Actions and Bulk Mutation](/docs/topics/RichTableViewsActions) | `RowAction`, `SelectionDef`, `BulkMutateDef`, `ActionResult`, `IdempotencyKey`, `WritePermit`. |
| [Renderers and Cell Popovers](/docs/topics/RichTableViewsRenderers) | `Render`, built-in renderer ids, `CellPopover`, custom renderers. |
| [Security Model](/docs/topics/RichTableViewsSecurity) | Sink allowlists, CSRF and loopback boundary, same-origin rules. |
| [JavaScript API](/docs/topics/RichTableViewsJavaScript) | `window.JuneauViews` namespaces and the asset load order. |
| [View Settings and Shareable Links](/docs/topics/RichTableViewsSettings) | The View Settings dialog, page-state persistence, Copy link and `?state=`. |

description:
A table card is authored as a JSON5 catalog in the body of `<@card type="datatables">`. The chrome parses it,
lifts it into the view contract and stamps the current contract versions (see
[Contract versions](/docs/topics/RichTableViews#contract-versions)). You never hand-author the version numbers.

```ftl
<@card type="datatables" id="pets" title="Pets">
{
  dataUrl: '/console/pets/data',
  dataMode: 'server',
  defaultOrder: [[0, 'asc']],
  columns: [
    { key: 'name',   label: 'Name',   searchType: 'text' },
    { key: 'status', label: 'Status', searchType: 'enum' },
    { key: 'price',  label: 'Price',  searchType: 'numeric', searchOperators: ['eq', 'gt', 'lt', 'between'] }
  ]
}
</@card>
```

## Catalog keys

`dataUrl` and `columns` are required; a catalog missing either fails the render with an `IllegalArgumentException`
naming the card. Each column is an object.

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `dataUrl` | Same-origin URL the table fetches its rows from. Must be a path, not an absolute cross-origin URL. |
| `columns[].key` (or `data`) | The row-data property this column reads. |
| `columns[].label` (or `title`) | The header text. |
| `columns[].searchType` | Makes the column searchable. One of the `SearchType` wire tokens below. A column without it is not searchable. |
| `columns[].searchOperators` | Optional allow-list narrowing the operators offered for the column. |
| `columns[].customOperators` | Optional `[{name, help}]` list of extra operators, with the help text the header popup shows. |
| `defaultOrder`, `ribbon`, `dataMode`, `rowType`, `pollIntervalMs`, `columnConfig`, `cleanAddress`, `primary` | Copied verbatim onto the view metadata when present. |

The `dataMode: "server"` setting selects server-side processing, driven by `juneau-datatables.js`. The host must
compose `DataTablesMixin`; see [the module table](/docs/topics/RichTableViews#modules-and-mixins).

The data endpoint behind `dataUrl` is an ordinary REST operation that answers a DataTables...

You never hand-author the version numbers.

description:
A view table can offer per-row actions (a row menu), row selection, and, as an independent opt-in, bulk mutation.
All of the types below live in `org.apache.juneau.console.views`.

## RowAction

A `RowAction` is one row-menu item. On activation `juneau-views.js` submits the declared `endpoint` with the
declared `method` as a JSON request carrying the process's CSRF token.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | Required. Stable action id. |
| `label`, `icon` | Menu text and an optional glyph name resolved by [the icon registry](/docs/topics/RichTableViewsIcons). |
| `endpoint` | The URL to submit to. May carry `{property}` tokens filled in from the row. |
| `method` | `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE`. |
| `confirm` | Optional confirmation prompt. |
| `form` | Optional form-source URL supplying input fields; may carry `{property}` tokens. Blank means a confirm-only action. |
| `present` | `page`, `dialog` or `inline` (`RowAction.Present`). |
| `onSuccess` | `redraw`, `mergeRow` or `navigate` (`RowAction.OnSuccess`). |
| `enabledWhen` | Row-state rules that must all match for the action to render enabled. |
| `visibleWhen` | Row-state rules that must all match for the action to be offered at all. |

```java
RowAction ack = RowAction.create("ack")
	.label("Acknowledge")
	.endpoint("servlet:/incidents/{id}/ack")
	.method(RowAction.Method.POST)
	.confirm("Acknowledge this incident?")
	.present(RowAction.Present.DIALOG)
	.onSuccess(RowAction.OnSuccess.MERGE_ROW)
	.enabledWhen("state", Op.NE, "resolved", "Already resolved");
```

Points worth knowing:

- `RowAction.Method` contains only the four non-safe methods, so a mutating action bound to `GET` cannot be
  expressed. On the server, mutating operations are checked for the same rule at startup.
- A `{property}` token that cannot be resolved from the row refuses the submission instead of sending a malformed
  request. A value with no token is used exactly as written.
- `enabledWhen` is presentation only. A gated acti...
summary: A view table can offer per-row actions (a row menu), row selection, and, as an independent opt-in, bulk mutation. All of the types below live in `org.apache.juneau.console.views`.
title: Row Actions and Bulk Mutation

description:
A `Render` (in `org.apache.juneau.console.views`) names how a column's value is painted into its cell. It has
an `id` that selects a renderer, an optional `meta` map of string parameters, and an optional `popover`.

## Built-in renderers

The ids in `SinkRenderAllowlist.BUILTIN_IDS` are the renderers the runtime ships:

`date`, `datetime`, `ts-zulu`, `bool`, `linked`, `truncate`, `json`, `decimal`, `tag`, `progress`, `pill`, `code`.

- `linked` builds an `href` from a template whose `{property}` tokens are filled from the row. Each substituted
  value is escaped, and the resulting URL is scheme-checked by the sink allowlist (see
  [Security Model](/docs/topics/RichTableViewsSecurity)).
- `pill` and `tag` render status chips using the same pill styling as `<@tag>` in the
  [chrome](/docs/topics/AdminConsoleChrome). A `pill` never emits `role="button"`.
- `edit:<actionId>` shows the value with a pencil that turns the cell into an input (`text`, `number` or `select`, via
  the `input` and `options` meta). Enter or leaving the field saves through the named row action, sending the edited
  column as `fields`; Escape or an unchanged value cancels without a request. A failed save keeps the input open with
  the error beside it. The pencil follows the action's `visibleWhen` and `enabledWhen`. It is a cell renderer only and
  is not on the sink allowlist.
- Dates render through `Intl.DateTimeFormat` in the browser, so they follow the user's locale.

## Custom renderers

Register a renderer before the view mounts. The definition is either a bare function (treated as the `display`
facet) or an object with `display`, `sort`, `filter`, `type` and `class` facets:

```js
JuneauViews.registerRenderer("stars", {
  display: function (cellData, rowData, meta) {
    const n = Number(cellData) || 0;
    return "★".repeat(n);   // display returns a markup string: escape anything that came from data
  },
  sort: function (cellData) { return Number(cellData) || 0; }
});
```

description:
The views toolkit is built so that an author mistake fails closed instead of opening an injection or CSRF hole.
This page collects the rules in one place.

## Sinks never take raw HTML

Every value the runtime paints goes through one of a small number of sinks:

| Sink | Rule |
|---|---|
| Plain text (`FieldFormat.TEXT`) | `textContent`. |
| `FieldFormat.MARKDOWN` | Parsed and copied node by node through an allowlist. Never `innerHTML`. |
| `FieldFormat.SANITIZED_HTML` | Parsed with `DOMParser` into an inert document; allowlisted elements and attributes are copied with `createElement`. Never serialized back to a string, so the mutation-XSS class cannot arise. |
| Links (`href`, `src`) | Scheme-checked. `javascript:`, `data:` and `vbscript:` are rejected by prefix, and a second colon-fallback rule rejects any value with a colon that is not an allowlisted absolute prefix (`http:`, `https:`, `mailto:` for `href`; `http:`, `https:` for `src`). The colon-fallback is the load-bearing rule: it still catches obfuscated spellings. |

`SANITIZED_HTML` does not relieve you of sanitizing: the contract is caller-sanitizes-first, with the runtime's
allowlist as a second layer.

## Render allowlist

Table-cell renderers are looked up in the client registry; an unknown id warns and falls back to the raw value.
Field-grid fill sinks are stricter. `SinkRenderAllowlist` accepts only its frozen built-in ids
(`date`, `datetime`, `ts-zulu`, `bool`, `linked`, `truncate`, `json`, `decimal`, `tag`, `progress`, `pill`, `code`),
and `CellPopover` fields are further limited to `SinkRenderAllowlist.POPOVER_TEXT_IDS`
(`date`, `bool`, `decimal`, `datetime`, `ts-zulu`). A `pill` on a fill sink is display only and never
emits `role="button"`.

## Populator allowlist

A [region](/docs/topics/RichTableViewsRegions) names a client-side populator function. `PopulatorAllowlist`
validates `RegionDef.populate` against the region's `allowedPopulators`, so a catalog cannot name an arbitrary
function; a b...
summary: The views toolkit is built so that an author mistake fails closed instead of opening an injection or CSRF hole. This page collects the rules in one place.
title: Security Model

description:
The runtime publishes everything on one global, `window.JuneauViews`. Each script adds its own members to that
object and none replaces another's, so the load order below is a contract rather than a preference.

## Asset load order

The `views` toolkit pack (`ToolkitPackRegistry`) emits these scripts in this order. A `<@page toolkit="views">`
page gets them automatically; a hand-built page must reproduce the order.

| # | Script (constant on `ViewsMixin`) | Adds |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `juneau-renders.js` (`RENDERS_JS_PATH`) | `registerRenderer`, `resolveRenderer`, the built-in renderers. |
| 2 | `juneau-icons.js` (`ICONS_JS_PATH`) | `icons`. |
| 3 | `juneau-search.js` (`SEARCH_JS_PATH`) | `search`, the column search-expression engine. |
| 4 | `juneau-pagestate.js` (`PAGESTATE_JS_PATH`) | `pageState`. |
| 5 | `juneau-urlstate.js` (`URLSTATE_JS_PATH`) | `urlState`, shareable-URL state and the View Settings Copy link button. |
| 6 | `juneau-ribbon.js` (`RIBBON_JS_PATH`) | `ribbon`. |
| 7 | `juneau-views.js` (`VIEWS_JS_PATH`) | The core: `init` and the table runtime. |
| 8 | `juneau-config.js` (`CONFIG_JS_PATH`) | `config`, `persistence`, `persistenceProviders`, `setPersistenceProvider`; the View Settings dialog. |
| 9 | `juneau-regions.js` (`REGIONS_JS_PATH`) | `regions`. Must come after `juneau-views.js`. |
| 10 | `juneau-helpers.js` (`HELPERS_JS_PATH`) | `helpers`, including the field grid. |

Stylesheets are `juneau-views.css` and `juneau-config.css`. jQuery, DataTables and `juneau-datatables.js` are not part
of the `views` pack; a datatables card loads them before it (see
[Card Asset Dependencies](/docs/topics/CardAssetDependencies)).

A page with the calendar widget lists `toolkit="views,calendar"` so `juneau-views.js` still loads before
`juneau-calendar.js`. The scripts are classpath resources under `org/apache/juneau/views/`.

description:
A view table lets each user adjust how a table looks and keep those choices, and lets them share what they are
looking at. These are two separate facilities that persist in different places.

## View Settings

The View Settings dialog (provided by `juneau-config.js`) has four tabs: View, Search, Sort and Options. It lets
the user change the visible columns, their labels, format and order, which columns are searchable and sortable,
the page size and wrapping.

- **Apply** commits the settings to the page-state store, keyed per table, so several tables on one page never
  overwrite each other. A reload restores them.
- Settings are stored through `JuneauViews.pageState` (see [JavaScript API](/docs/topics/RichTableViewsJavaScript)),
  not in the address bar.
- The dialog starts from the catalog defaults, and the saved blob is overlaid on top of them.
- Saved view names have a maximum length, and `Default` is a reserved name.

For the dialog's tabs, the `schemaVersion` guard, settings applied on load, the Sort tab, auto-refresh and the Copy link
button, see [Datatable View Settings](/docs/topics/DatatableViewSettings).

To keep settings somewhere other than browser `localStorage`, install a store with
`JuneauViews.pageState.useStore({getItem, setItem, removeItem})`, or supply a persistence provider through
`JuneauViews.setPersistenceProvider(provider)`.

## Copy link and shareable state

Copy link builds a URL for what the user is currently looking at: the selected tab, the active filters and the
sort. The state is one readable `?state=` query parameter, placed directly in the address bar.

- `JuneauViews.urlState.buildShareUrl(location, state)` always includes `?state=`, even when the clean-address
  option is on.
- `JuneauViews.urlState.copy(navigator, text)` writes to the clipboard and resolves `true` or `false`; it never
  throws where the Clipboard API is absent or denied.
- The catalog's `cleanAddress` key keeps the live address bar free of `?state=`; Copy link...

title: View Settings and Shareable Links

description:
A region is an empty, framework-owned container whose body is drawn by a named JavaScript function (a
populator) instead of server-emitted markup. The framework owns the container, its identity, its lifecycle and its
cancellation; the populator owns everything inside it.

There are exactly three region types, the `RegionDef` constants:

| Constant | Where it lives |
|---|---|
| `TYPE_ROW_DETAIL` (`row-detail`) | Inside a table row's expandable detail panel. |
| `TYPE_CARD_BODY` (`card-body`) | In the body of a card. |
| `TYPE_TAB_BODY` (`tab-body`) | In a tab's body; lazy by default. |

## Declaring a region

`RegionDef` (in `org.apache.juneau.console.views`) is the server-side descriptor. `RegionDef.CONTRACT_VERSION`
is `"1"` and is independent of the view, action, bulk and slot versions.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | Unique within the host. |
| `populate` | Name of the client populator, or `null` for the built-in `default`. A name, not a function, so a server-side allowlist can constrain it. |
| `type` | One of the three types above. Usually set by the enclosing host. |
| `dataUrl` | Same-origin path the declarative default fetches from. `null` means no declared fetch. |
| `params` | Request parameters appended to `dataUrl`. Values may not be nested maps and keys may not collide with `dataUrl`'s own query string. |
| `renderer` | The `JuneauViews.helpers` function the default populate paints with, for example `field-grid`. |
| `lazy` | Defer the first populate until visible. Defaults to `false` for row-detail and card-body, `true` for tab-body (`effectiveLazy()`). |
| `refreshMs` | Auto-refresh interval. A value below `RegionDef.MIN_REFRESH_MS` is clamped up to it (5000 ms on the client). |
| `fields` | The field catalog for card and tab regions (`RegionDef.Field`: `label`, `render`, `href`, `format`, `span`, `actions`). A row-detail region must not declare one. |
| `titleFields` | Title keys the chrome's title painter may read. Blank entries are reje...
summary: A region is an empty, framework-owned container whose body is drawn by a named JavaScript function (a populator) instead of server-emitted markup. The framework owns the container, its identity, its lifecycle and its cancellation; the populator owns everything inside it.

description:
`juneau-icons.js` is a dependency-free icon registry. It maps an icon name to inline SVG that references one
in-document symbol sprite, using symbol ids of the form `juneau-sym-{stem}`.

## Sprite layers

Every chrome glyph resolves through up to three sprite layers; the first hit wins.

| Layer | Source |
|---|---|
| per-icon override | A small sprite of a few names you want to change. |
| replacement | Your own full or partial icon set. |
| shipped | Juneau's own set, `juneau-symbols.svg` (`ViewsMixin.SYMBOLS_SVG_PATH`). |

All three use the same `juneau-sym-{stem}` symbol ids. A name present in none of them draws nothing.

Configure the layers once per page, before the chrome first draws, with attributes on the script tag:

```html
<script src="/console/juneau-icons.js"
        data-juneau-icon-replacement="/my-set.svg"
        data-juneau-icon-override="/my-overrides.svg"></script>
```

or with an equivalent script call:

```js
JuneauViews.icons.sprites({ replacementUrl: "/my-set.svg", overrideUrl: "/my-overrides.svg" });
```

`sprites(...)` returns a `Promise` reporting, per layer, whether it loaded, failed or was absent, and per stem which
layer won. The page paints whether or not you await it. A layer that fails to load (including a blocked
cross-origin fetch) is skipped and the other layers fill in. A call after first paint is ignored.

## Material Symbols

The optional Material Symbols Outlined sprite is served at `ViewsMixin.SYMBOLS_MATERIAL_SVG_PATH`. Select it as the
replacement layer with `JuneauViews.icons.pack("material")` or `data-juneau-icon-pack="material"`. Stems the
Material file does not carry fall back to the shipped glyph. An explicit `replacementUrl` wins over the pack.

## Registering your own icons

```js
JuneauViews.icons.registerIcon("petstore-paw", "<svg viewBox='0 0 24 24'>...</svg>");
JuneauViews.icons.resolveIcon("petstore-paw");   // markup, or null when unknown
```

`registerIcon` adds an icon that your application draws itself; ...
summary: `juneau-icons.js` is a dependency-free icon registry. It maps an icon name to inline SVG that references one in-document symbol sprite, using symbol ids of the form `juneau-sym-{stem}`.
title: Icons and Sprites

description:
The terminal-view region shows the progress and result of a multi-step run: a summary card with a headline and
failures first, a list of steps with their state and duration, and a strip of colour blocks per test suite that
you can hover or focus for a tooltip. It reads a stream of small, versioned **events** from an endpoint, or from
events your own code hands to it, and reduces them to one model on the client.

You can show one in three ways:

| Where | How |
|---|---|
| A console page card | `<@card type="terminal-view" id="run">{ contractVersion: '1', terminalView: {...} }</@card>` |
| A views page region | `TerminalViewDef.forMixin(...).toRegion()` in a `RegionTable` |
| A table row detail | A `datatables` catalog `detail.region` with `populate: 'terminal-view'` and `params` |

The event types and the report readers live in their own small module, `juneau-terminal-report` (package
`org.apache.juneau.terminal.report`: `TerminalEvent`, `TerminalViewChecks`, `ReportReaders` and the readers), which has
no dependency on the REST server. A producer such as a build tool can depend on it alone. The rest of the server
half ships in `juneau-console-views` (`org.apache.juneau.console.views`), which depends on
`juneau-terminal-report`; the client half is `juneau-terminal-view.js`, part of the `views` toolkit pack. It pairs naturally with the [Terminal Region](/docs/topics/TerminalRegion): the
terminal view summarizes, the terminal holds the raw output, and a test block can link to the terminal offset it came from.

```json
{
  "contractVersion": "1",
  "events": [ { "ev": "step", "seq": 1, "id": "build", "title": "mvn package" } ],
  "next": "k3x9ab.1",
  "more": false,
  "terminal": false
}
```

| Page member | Rules |
|---|---|
| `contractVersion` | Required. Exactly `"1"`; anything else is fatal (E-RV-2). |

description:
The terminal region shows a command's output the way a terminal would: colours, bold, cursor movement, progress bars
that redraw in place, and full-screen boxes. The server sends the command's raw bytes, unchanged, and
[xterm.js](https://xtermjs.org/) renders them in the browser. Use it when the output only makes sense on a terminal.

The region lives in its own module, `juneau-terminal-region` (package `org.apache.juneau.terminal.region`).
It is opt-in: add the module and nothing else changes. It depends on `juneau-console-views` and on the xterm.js
WebJar (`org.webjars.npm:xterm__xterm`, pinned at 6.0.0).

## A console page card

```html
<@card type="terminal" id="build" title="Build">
{
    contractVersion: '1',
    terminal: {
        bytesUrl: '/runs/juneau-terminal/r42/bytes',
        eventsUrl: '/runs/juneau-terminal-view/r42/events',
        refreshMs: 1000,
        title: 'mvn test',
        tailBytes: 2097152
    }
}
</@card>
```

| Key | Rules |
|---|---|
| `bytesUrl` | Required. A same-origin path, with no scheme, no leading `//`, no `..` segment and no `{`. |
| `eventsUrl` | Optional. A terminal-view events endpoint over the same run. It gives the steps their offsets and the badge its exit code. |
| `refreshMs` | Optional. The poll interval while the command runs. Values below 1000 are raised to 1000; a value of 0 or less is an error. |
| `title` | Optional. Shown in the toolbar. |
| `tailBytes` | Optional, 1 to 1 GiB, default 2 MiB. On first load only the last `tailBytes` are fetched; **Load all** fetches the rest. |

The card takes its options as the body only; `src=` and `template=` are rejected. The page needs no `toolkit=`: the
card pulls the `terminal` toolkit pack, which brings `views` and `xterm` with it. From Java, `TerminalDef.forMixin("build", "/runs", "r42")` builds the
same options.

description:
A row job is an async job started for one table row, from the row itself or from its expanded detail panel. The
browser side is `JuneauViews.jobs` in `juneau-views.js`, with `helpers.jobButton` as a ready-made button and the
console's [job-log region](/docs/topics/JobLogCard#in-a-row-detail-region) as a declarative form. The server side is
`JobKeyLedger` and `RowJobSubmit` (package `org.apache.juneau.console.views`), which bind each submit key to the
row it was issued for. The job itself is an ordinary [async job](/docs/topics/RichTableViewsAsyncJobs).

## Running a job

```js
const handle = JuneauViews.jobs.run({
  el: button,                                   // inside the row or its detail panel
  endpoint: "/ops/species/{id}/restock",
  action: "restock-species",
  envelope: "action",
  keyUrl: "/ops/species/{id}/key",
  fields: { count: 3 },
  trigger: button,
  hooks: {
    onProgress: line => log.append(line),
    onEnd: ({ state, result, error }) => console.info(state, result, error)
  }
});
await handle.done;
```

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `el` | Required. An element inside the row, or inside the row's detail panel. It names the row, its table and its CSRF token. |
| `endpoint` | Required. A same-origin path template. `{id}` is replaced with the row id, URL-encoded; any other `{token}` is refused. |
| `method` | `POST` (default) or `PUT`. |
| `action` | The action id. Required with `envelope: "action"`; also names the job on the bus and in the row marker. When the view declares a row action with this id, only its `label` is used. |
| `envelope` | `"flat"` (default) sends `{action, ...fields, idempotencyKey}`; `"action"` sends `{action, targetId, idempotencyKey, fields}`. |
| `idempotencyKey` | A key to send. Otherwise give `keyUrl`. |
| `keyUrl` | A same-origin key-endpoint template (`{id}` only). The key is fetched and checked before the submit. |
| `fields` | The values to send, already resolved. In the flat envelope `action`, `targetId` and `id...

description:
The console message bus carries small JSON values between your server code and the pages of a console. The server
publishes to a **topic**; every page that asked for the topic receives the value, and a page that connects later
receives the last retained value straight away. Pages can also publish back on a few topics you allow. Use it to push
live state (job counts, alerts, a terminal's new bytes) to a page without the page polling for it.

The bus is split over three opt-in modules. Add only what you need:

| Module | Package | Adds |
|---|---|---|
| `juneau-console-bus` | `org.apache.juneau.console.bus` | `ServerBus`, `BusPolicy`, and the session POST and SSE stream (`BusEventsMixin`). Server to page only. |
| `juneau-console-bus-websocket` | `org.apache.juneau.console.bus.websocket` | The Jakarta WebSocket transport (`BusWebSockets`). The only transport that carries page to server frames. |
| `juneau-terminal-bus` | `org.apache.juneau.terminal.bus` | `TerminalInput` and `TerminalNudges`, which connect the [terminal region](/docs/topics/TerminalRegion) to the bus. |

`juneau-console-bus` depends on `juneau-rest-server`. The WebSocket module adds the bus module and the Jakarta
WebSocket API; the servlet container supplies the implementation (for example Jetty's
`jetty-ee11-websocket-jakarta-server` or Tomcat's `tomcat-embed-websocket`).

## The pieces

| Type | Role |
|---|---|
| `ServerBus` | Holds the retained topic values and the sessions that bridge them to pages. Create one per application and `close()` it when the application stops. |
| `BusPolicy` | Says what may flow, in which direction, to whom. Everything not allowed is denied. |
| `BusEventsMixin` | Interface you add to a REST resource. It exposes `POST /juneau-bus/session` and `GET /juneau-bus/stream/{sessionId}` relative to the resource. |

description:
The View Settings dialog lets a user tailor a datatable view (the `juneau-console-views` table card) and keep
those choices across reloads. This page covers the dialog's tabs, how settings persist and are applied, the Sort
tab, auto-refresh, the per-column search announcer and the Copy link button. For the catalog keys that configure a
view see [Rich Table Views](/docs/topics/RichTableViews); for the page-state store and the `?state=` URL codec see
[View Settings and Shareable Links](/docs/topics/RichTableViewsSettings).

## Dialog tabs

The dialog has four tabs: **View** (columns: visibility, order, label, format), **Search** (which columns take part
in the search box), **Sort** and **Options**. The tabs follow the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern: each tab carries
`aria-selected` and `aria-controls`, only the active tab is in the Tab order, and Left, Right, Home and End move
between tabs. Every per-row control (visible, move up/down, label, format and so on) has an `aria-label` that names
its column.

### Restricting the tabs

A view can show fewer tabs with `columnConfig.tabs` in its catalog:

```json
{ "columnConfig": { "tabs": ["columns", "sort"] } }
```

The names are `columns`, `search`, `sort` and `options`; `columns` is the tab shown on screen as **View**. An empty or
unknown list falls back to all four tabs. Settings that belong to a hidden tab are not read from, applied from or
written to the stored settings for that view.

## Persistence

Apply writes one settings blob per table into the page-state store (browser `localStorage` by default). The blob
carries a `schemaVersion`, currently **2**. When the stored blob has a different (older, newer or missing)
`schemaVersion`, or the sort is in the old string-array form, the runtime deletes it, falls back to the catalog
defaults and shows a one-time notice ("your saved settings were reset"). It never tries to migrate a blob it does not
recognise.

description:
Juneau provides both server-side and client-side support for the [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/), a JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol that lets AI assistants and agents discover and invoke external **tools**, **prompts**, and **resources**.

Two protocol revisions are supported side-by-side as separate, revision-bound Maven modules: `2025-06-18` and `2026-07-28` (the current revision). A client/server pair picks one revision at compile time — see [Choosing your MCP setup](/docs/topics/JuneauMcpChoosingSetup) for the full comparison, why the MCP ecosystem is 9 artifacts (3 shared cores + 6 per-revision adapters) rather than 6 independent ones, and why the two revisions are maintained differently going forward.

## Where to start

- **[MCP Quickstart](/docs/topics/JuneauMcpQuickstart)** — a working server and client talking to each other in about 5 minutes.
- **[Choosing your MCP setup](/docs/topics/JuneauMcpChoosingSetup)** — protocol revision, dedicated servlet vs mixin, plain vs Spring Boot.
- **[MCP Recipes](/docs/topics/JuneauMcpRecipes)** — copy-pasteable snippets for tools, prompts, resources, resource templates, completions, error handling, elicitation, and subscriptions.

## Deep reference

- **[juneau-rest-server-mcp](/docs/topics/JuneauRestServerMcp)** — full server-side API reference: capabilities, pagination, notifications, cache hints, tracing, Multi-Round-Trip Requests, elicitation, and subscriptions.
- **[juneau-rest-client-mcp](/docs/topics/JuneauRestClientMcp)** — full client-side API reference: the duplex server-request channel, auth, and response caching.
- **[juneau-bean-mcp-v20250618](/docs/topics/JuneauBeanMcp)** — the MCP wire-bean catalog underlying both the server and client modules.
summary: Juneau provides both server-side and client-side support for the [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/), a JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol that lets AI assistants and agents discover and invoke external **tools**, **prompts**, and **resources**.
title: MCP (Model Context Protocol)

description:
Three independent decisions determine which classes you extend/implement and which Maven artifacts you depend on. They can be mixed freely — e.g. `2026-07-28` + mixin + Spring Boot is a perfectly normal combination.

## Module shape: 3 shared cores, 6 per-revision adapters

The MCP ecosystem is **9 Maven artifacts, not 6 independent ones**. Three of them are revision-neutral **cores** — each has zero compile-time knowledge of `2025-06-18` vs `2026-07-28` — and each core carries two thin **adapter** modules on top, one per protocol revision:

```
juneau-bean-jsonrpc                 JSON-RPC 2.0 envelope (revision-neutral)
├── juneau-bean-mcp-v20250618           2025-06-18 wire beans
└── juneau-bean-mcp-v20260728           2026-07-28 wire beans

juneau-rest-server-mcp              server dispatch core (revision-neutral)
├── juneau-rest-server-mcp-v20250618
└── juneau-rest-server-mcp-v20260728

juneau-rest-client-mcp              client core (revision-neutral)
├── juneau-rest-client-mcp-v20250618
└── juneau-rest-client-mcp-v20260728
```

The three decisions below only concern which **adapter** coordinate you pick per side — the neutral cores come along transitively; you don't depend on or configure them directly.

**Why a separate artifact per revision, instead of one artifact with a runtime revision switch:** Maven/Gradle dependency resolution happens at build time, so keeping a `2025-06-18`-only consumer off `2026-07-28`-only dependencies has to be a compile-time artifact choice, not a runtime flag. The `2026-07-28` server adapter alone pulls in `juneau-rest-server-reactive` (reactive-streams SSE, for subscriptions), `juneau-rest-server-auth-oauth` (OAuth 2.1), and `juneau-rest-server-auth-jwt` (JWT) — none of which land on the classpath of a `2025-06-18`-only deployment.

**Why the two adapters keep diverging in size rather than converging:** `2025-06-18` is maintained for bug fixes and spec-correctness only, indefinitely. All new MCP capability work — Multi-Roun...

`juneau-rest-server-mcp` is a **revision-neutral core** for exposing a [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) JSON-RPC endpoint on `juneau-rest-server`. - A **revision SPI** (`McpRevision`) that a protocol revision implements — the neutral core dispatches through it without knowing what's on the other side.
- A drop-in **servlet** (`McpRestServlet`, concretely `org.apache.juneau.rest.server.mcp.v20250618.McpRestServlet`) for the common case of "expose an MCP endpoint at `POST /mcp`".

`juneau-rest-client-mcp` is the revision-neutral MCP client core built on `juneau-rest-client`, with two dated adapters: `juneau-rest-client-mcp-v20250618` and `juneau-rest-client-mcp-v20260728`. ## Overview

The client stack is split exactly like the server stack:

- `juneau-rest-client-mcp` - neutral transport/auth/cache/duplex seams centered on `AbstractMcpClient`.
- `juneau-rest-client-mcp-v20250618` - typed facade for MCP `2025-06-18`.
- `juneau-rest-client-mcp-v20260728` - typed facade for MCP `2026-07-28`.

The neutral core sends raw JSON-RPC (`JsonRpcRequest`/`JsonRpcResponse`) and leaves revision-specific `_meta`/header details to dated adapters.

Juneau 10 ships **two** REST client stacks in the same release. Both are supported; they differ in

See the guide: [Call an existing REST API with a typed proxy](/docs/guides/TypedProxyClient)

:::tip Which client?
`juneau-rest-client` (`org.apache.juneau.rest.client.RestClient`) is the recommended REST client. It is generally
available in 10.0.0, transport-agnostic, and uses the JDK `HttpClient` by default. `juneau-rest-client-classic`
(`org.apache.juneau.rest.client.classic.RestClient`, Apache HttpClient 4.5) stays supported and is not deprecated; it is
the stable choice for existing users. See [Choosing a REST Client](/docs/topics/ChoosingARestClient).
:::

| | Next-Generation (NG) client | Classic client |
|---|---|---|
| Maven artifact | `juneau-rest-client` | `juneau-rest-client-classic` |
| Package | `org.apache.juneau.rest.client` | `org.apache.juneau.rest.client.classic` |
| HTTP library | Pluggable [transport](/docs/topics/HttpTransportAdapters); JDK `HttpClient` by default (no third-party dependencies) | Apache HttpClient 4.5 only |
| Extends `HttpClient` | No | Yes (`implements org.apache.http.client.HttpClient`) |
| HTTP types | `org.apache.juneau.http.*` | `org.apache.juneau.http.classic.*` (HttpCore-based) |
| Mock client | `org.apache.juneau.rest.mock.MockRestClient` | `org.apache.juneau.rest.mock.classic.MockRestClient` |
| SSRF guard for `@Remote` / `@Url` | Yes, with per-hop redirect re-validation ([NG Security](/docs/topics/NgClientSecurity)) | Yes (classic guard classes) |
| Stability | Generally available in 10.0.0; the recommended client | Stable, unchanged from 9.x; supported, not deprecated |

description: The classic Juneau REST client delegates authentication to the underlying Apache HTTP Client, so you configure it with HTTP Client APIs or the builder shortcuts. ## When to use it Use this when the server you call requires credentials: BASIC with a one-line shortcut, or FORM-based and OIDC logins by customizing the HTTP client. :::warning Classic-client-only The auth-shortcut convenience methods shown on these pages (such as basicAuth(...)) are builder methods on the classic RestClient.Builder (org.apache.juneau.rest.client.classic), which wraps Apache HttpClient 4.5. The [Next-Generation REST Client](/docs/topics/NextGenRestClient) has **no** equivalent auth-shortcut methods at all — it has no dependency on Apache HttpClient, so authentication must instead be configured on the transport you choose (for example, the native Apache HC 4.5/5, OkHttp, or JDK `HttpClient` builder) before wrapping it in an `HttpTransport`. ::: ## Example ```java import org.apache.juneau.rest.client.classic.*; public class BasicAuthExample { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { // Create a client that performs BASIC authentication using the specified user/pw. try (RestClient client = RestClient.create() .json() .basicAuth("localhost", 8080, "me", "mypassword") .build()) { System.out.println("Built RestClient"); } } } ``` ## Options | Mechanism | How | |---|---| | BASIC | `basicAuth(host, port, user, pw)` on the builder | | FORM-based | Override `createHttpClient()` and log in before returning the client | | OIDC | Override `createHttpClient()` and run the redirect handshake before returning the client | ## BASIC authentication The basicAuth() method can be used to quickly ena...

description:
:::tip Which client?
`juneau-rest-client` (`org.apache.juneau.rest.client.RestClient`) is the recommended REST client. It is generally
available in 10.0.0, transport-agnostic, and uses the JDK `HttpClient` by default. `juneau-rest-client-classic`
(`org.apache.juneau.rest.client.classic.RestClient`, Apache HttpClient 4.5) stays supported and is not deprecated; it is
the stable choice for existing users. See [Choosing a REST Client](/docs/topics/ChoosingARestClient).
:::

Juneau 10.0 promotes the next-generation REST client and HTTP type stack to the **canonical names**
under `org.apache.juneau.rest.client.*`, `org.apache.juneau.rest.mock.*`, and
`org.apache.juneau.http.*`. The pre-existing Apache HttpClient 4.5–based stack ships unchanged under
`.classic` packages and the new `juneau-rest-client-classic` Maven module — see
[V10 Migration Guide](/docs/topics/V10MigrationGuide) for the import-rename table.

See the guide: [Call an existing REST API with a typed proxy](/docs/guides/TypedProxyClient)

The next-generation stack:

- Uses **only JDK types** in its API surface ([org.apache.juneau.http](pathname:///site/apidocs/org/apache/juneau/http/package-summary.html)). No `org.apache.http.*` on
  any signature.
- Introduces an `HttpTransport` abstraction so you can plug in **any HTTP client**
  (Apache HC 4.5, Apache HC 5, JDK `HttpClient`, OkHttp, Jetty, or a custom transport)
  without changing user code.
- Replaces 40+ Apache HC–specific builder methods on the classic `RestClient.Builder` with a
  small, focused builder. Transport-specific configuration lives on the **transport builder**,
  not on `RestClient.Builder`.

---

## Package Layout

| Package | Module | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `org.apache.juneau.http` | `juneau-rest-common` | JDK-native HTTP types (`HttpHeader`, `HttpPart`, `HttpBody`, status types, ~73 RFC-named headers, ~50 named response types, multipart, remote-proxy annotations). No `httpcore` dependency. |
| `org.apache.juneau.rest.client` | `juneau...

description:
A request is built fluently from a [`RestClient`](pathname:///site/apidocs/org/apache/juneau/rest/client/RestClient.html)
verb method and executed with `run()`. Each verb (`get`, `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`, `head`, and
`request(method, url)`) returns a [`RestRequest`](pathname:///site/apidocs/org/apache/juneau/rest/client/RestRequest.html).

```java
RestClient client = RestClient.builder()
    .rootUrl("https://api.example.com")
    .serializer(Json5Serializer.create().build())
    .parser(Json5Parser.create().build())
    .build();

try (var resp = client.post("/users/{id}/notes")
        .pathData("id", 42)
        .queryData("notify", true)
        .header("X-Trace", "abc")
        .body(new Note("hello"))
        .timeout(Duration.ofSeconds(5))
        .run()) {
    resp.assertOk();
}
```

## Request parts

| Method | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `header(name, value)` / `headers(...)` | Request headers. |
| `queryData(name, value)` | Query-string parameters. |
| `formData(name, value)` | `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` form fields. |
| `pathData(name, value)` | Substitutes `{name}` in the URL path. |
| `timeout(Duration)` | Per-request timeout. |
| `requestId(String)` | Overrides the generated `X-Request-Id`. |

Defaults set on the builder (`header`, `headers`, `queryData`) apply to every request made by that client.

## Request bodies

| Method | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `body(HttpBody)` | Sent as-is. |
| `body(Object)` | Runs the [body converter](/docs/topics/NgBodyConverters) chain first (`HttpBody`, `InputStream`, `byte[]`, `File`, plus any you registered); if none matches, the object is serialized with the client's default serializer. With no default serializer configured, an `IllegalStateException` is thrown. |
| `bodyString(String)` | Sent as `text/plain`. |
| `streamBodyEntity(RecordStreamBody)` | Streams a record sequence without buffering it. See [Streaming Cursors](/docs/topics/StreamingCursors). |

## Running the request

description:
`run()` returns a [`RestResponse`](pathname:///site/apidocs/org/apache/juneau/rest/client/RestResponse.html).
It is `Closeable` and holds the connection until closed, so always use try-with-resources.

```java
try (var resp = client.get("/users/42").run()) {
    int status = resp.getStatusCode();
    String type = resp.header("Content-Type").orElse("unknown");
    User user = resp.body().as(User.class);
}
```

## Status

`getStatusCode()`, `getReasonPhrase()`, and `getRequestId()` (the `X-Request-Id` that was sent).
`assertOk()` and `assertStatus(int)` throw `RestCallException` (with `getStatusCode()`) when the status
does not match.

## Headers

`getHeaders()` and `getFirstHeader(name)` return the raw values. `header(name)` returns a typed
[`ResponseHeader`](pathname:///site/apidocs/org/apache/juneau/rest/client/ResponseHeader.html):

| Accessor | Returns |
|---|---|
| `isPresent()`, `getName()` | Presence and name. |
| `getValue()`, `orElse(String)`, `asOptional()` | Raw string value. |
| `getValues()`, `asCsvList()` | Repeated or comma-separated values. |
| `asInteger()`, `asLong()`, `asBoolean()` | Numeric and boolean parsing. |
| `asZonedDateTime()` | HTTP-date parsing. |
| `asUri()`, `asEntityTag()`, `asEntityTags()`, `asStringRanges()` | Structured header types. |

See also [Typed Response Header Accessors](/docs/topics/NextGenRestClient#typed-response-header-accessors).

## Body

`body()` returns a [`ResponseBody`](pathname:///site/apidocs/org/apache/juneau/rest/client/ResponseBody.html).
The body can be consumed once.

| Method | Result |
|---|---|
| `asString()` | Decoded text. |
| `asBytes()` / `readAllBytes()` | Entire body as a byte array. |
| `asStream()` | The raw `InputStream`; you must close it. |
| `as(Class<T>)` | Parses into a POJO using the parser selected by the response `Content-Type`. Throws a 415 `UnsupportedMediaType` if no registered parser matches. See [Content-Type Negotiation](/docs/topics/ContentTypeNegotiation). |

description:
A [`BodyConverter<T>`](pathname:///site/apidocs/org/apache/juneau/rest/client/BodyConverter.html) turns an object
passed to `RestRequest.body(Object)` into a transport body *before* the client falls back to the default
serializer.

```java
public interface BodyConverter<T> {
    boolean canConvert(Object o);
    TransportBody convert(Object o) throws Exception;

    static <T> BodyConverter<T> of(Class<T> type, ThrowingConverter<T> fn);
}
```

## Built-in converters

`RestClient.DEFAULT_BODY_CONVERTERS` handles, in order: `HttpBody`, `InputStream`, `byte[]`, and `File`.
Anything else is serialized by the client's default serializer.

## Registering your own

```java
RestClient client = RestClient.builder()
    .bodyConverter(BodyConverter.of(Path.class, p -> TransportBody.of(FileBody.of(p.toFile()))))
    .build();

client.put("/upload").body(Path.of("data.bin")).run().close();
```

| Builder method | Effect |
|---|---|
| `bodyConverter(...)` | **Prepends** converters, so they win over the defaults and keep them as fallbacks. |
| `bodyConverters(...)` | **Replaces** the whole list, including the built-in converters. |

The first converter whose `canConvert` returns `true` is used.

## When to use one

- Sending a type you do not want routed through Juneau marshalling (streams, files, pre-encoded data).
- Adding a transport body for a domain type (for example, a buffer with a specific content type).

For serializing beans, prefer configuring a serializer rather than writing a converter.

description:
`RestResponse.assertThat()` returns a `ResponseAssertion`
(package `org.apache.juneau.rest.client.assertion`) for fluent checks. Failures throw `AssertionError`,
so they work directly in JUnit tests.

```java
try (var resp = client.get("/users/42").run()) {
    resp.assertThat()
        .isOk()
        .header("Content-Type").contains("json").and()
        .header("ETag").isPresent().and()
        .body().contains("\"id\":42").and();
}
```

## ResponseAssertion

| Method | Checks |
|---|---|
| `statusCode()` | Returns an integer assertion on the status. |
| `isOk()` | Status is 2xx. |
| `isClientError()` / `isServerError()` | Status is 4xx / 5xx. |
| `header(name)` | Switches to a `ResponseHeaderAssertion`. |
| `body()` | Switches to a `ResponseBodyAssertion`. |
| `and()` | Returns to the parent assertion. |

## ResponseHeaderAssertion

`isPresent()`, `isAbsent()`, `equals(String)`, `contains(String)`, `startsWith(String)`,
`integerEquals(int)`, `and()`.

## ResponseBodyAssertion

`equals(String)`, `contains(String)`, `startsWith(String)`, `isEmpty()`, `isNotEmpty()`, `and()`.

Body assertions read the body, so they consume it. Use them instead of, not in addition to,
`body().as(...)` on the same response.

## Assertions versus exceptions

- `assertThat()` is for tests: it throws `AssertionError`.
- `assertOk()` / `assertStatus(int)` on the response are for application code: they throw
  `RestCallException`, which you can catch and inspect with `getStatusCode()`.
summary: `RestResponse.assertThat()` returns a `ResponseAssertion` (package `org.apache.juneau.rest.client.assertion`) for fluent checks. Failures throw `AssertionError`, so they work directly in JUnit tests.

description:
The next-generation engine adds a family of declarative capabilities to the
[REST proxy](/docs/topics/RestProxies) annotations (`@Remote`, `@RemoteOp`, and the verb
annotations `@RemoteGet` / `@RemotePost` / `@RemotePut` / `@RemoteDelete` / `@RemotePatch`). This
page covers those capabilities; the client itself is described in the
[Next-Generation REST Client](/docs/topics/NextGenRestClient) overview.

:::warning Mostly next-gen engine only
Most features on this page are honored **only** by the next-generation proxy engine obtained via
`RestClient.remote(MyProxy.class)` → `RemoteClient`. The classic engine obtained via
`RestClient.getRemote(...)` ignores those annotation members; where an attribute is visible on a
shared annotation, its Javadoc states that the classic engine currently ignores it. The one
exception is [dynamic URLs and base overrides](#dynamic-urls-and-base-overrides) (`@Url` /
`baseUrl()`), which the classic engine also honors, with the same SSRF guardrail.
:::

```java
// Next-gen proxy — honors everything on this page.
MyProxy proxy = client.remote(MyProxy.class);

// Classic proxy — also honors @Url / baseUrl() (see below); ignores the other next-gen-only
// members on this page.
MyProxy classic = client.getRemote(MyProxy.class, "https://api.example.com");
```

## Constant Part Values

`@Remote` (interface) and `@RemoteOp` / the verb annotations (method) can declare **always-applied
constant** headers, query parameters, and form-data fields that are emitted on every call — with no
corresponding method parameter and no dummy `null` argument.

- Interface-level: `@Remote(headers=…, queryData=…, formData=…)`.
- Method-level: `@RemoteOp(headers=…, queryData=…, formData=…)` (and the verb annotations).
- `headers` use the `"Name: value"` form; `queryData` / `formData` use the `"name=value"` form.
- All values resolve through `VarResolver.DEFAULT` (e.g. `"$S{mySystemProperty}"`).
- A method-level constant of the same name **takes precedence over** an...

description: ## Overview The canonical `RestClient` in [org.apache.juneau.rest.client](pathname:///site/apidocs/org/apache/juneau/rest/client/package-summary.html) is transport-agnostic. Every HTTP call is routed through an `HttpTransport` SPI, which is responsible for executing a fully-resolved `TransportRequest` and returning a `TransportResponse`. ``` RestClient → HttpTransport → (Apache HC 4.5 / Apache HC 5 / OkHttp / Jetty / JDK / Mock) ``` `RestClient`'s POJO marshalling, remote proxies, interceptors, error-code handling, and logging are all independent of which transport is in use. Swapping transports requires one line of configuration. --- ## Default Transport The built-in `JavaHttpTransport` — backed by the JDK's `java.net.http.HttpClient` — is the default. It is part of the `juneau-rest-client` artifact and requires no additional dependencies on Java 11+. For most applications it is the right starting point. ```java import org.apache.juneau.marshall.json5.*; import org.apache.juneau.rest.client.*; // No transport module needed — JavaHttpTransport is picked up automatically. RestClient client = RestClient.builder() .serializer(Json5Serializer.DEFAULT) .parser(Json5Parser.DEFAULT) .rootUrl("https://api.example.com") .build(); ``` ### JavaHttpTransport JavaHttpTransport wraps a JDK `java.net.http.HttpClient`. ## Maven Dependencies

Add the Juneau transport module and Apache HttpClient 4.5 to your project:

```xml
<!-- Juneau transport adapter -->
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.apache.juneau</groupId>
    <artifactId>juneau-rest-client-apache-httpclient-45</artifactId>
    <version>${juneau.version}</version>
</dependency>

<!-- Apache HttpClient 4.5 (transitive from the adapter, pinned here for clarity) -->
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.apache.httpcomponents</groupId>
    <artifactId>httpclient</artifactId>
    <version>4.5.14</version>
</dependency>
```

The Juneau adapter module declares `httpclient:4.5.14` as a dependency, so the second block can
be omitted if you are happy with the version the adapter brings in.

---

## Overview

`juneau-rest-client-apache-httpclient-45` provides an `HttpTransport` implementation backed by
**Apache HttpClient 4.5.x** (`org.apache.httpcomponents:httpclient`). Consider it when:

- Your project already pulls in Apache HttpClient 4.5 and you want a single shared client

- You need mature, battle-tested connection pooling, proxy support, cookie management, or

- You are migrating an existing HC 4.5 integration to the Juneau REST client API incrementally.

The transport is auto-discovered via `ServiceLoader` when the module is on the classpath. An
explicit `.transport(...)` call always wins over auto-discovery.

## Overview

`juneau-rest-client-apache-httpclient-50` provides an `HttpTransport` implementation backed by
**Apache HttpClient 5.x** (`org.apache.httpcomponents.client5:httpclient5`). Consider it when:

- You are starting a new project and want the latest Apache HttpComponents API.
- You need HTTP/2 support within the Apache HC ecosystem.
- You are migrating an existing HC 5 integration to the Juneau REST client API.

The transport uses the **classic (synchronous)** `CloseableHttpClient` execution path from HC 5.
Async-only HC 5 features (e.g., `CloseableHttpAsyncClient`) are not exposed; route calls through
the transport interface as usual.

The transport is auto-discovered via `ServiceLoader` when the module is on the classpath. An
explicit `.transport(...)` call always wins over auto-discovery.

## Overview

`juneau-rest-client-okhttp` provides an `HttpTransport` implementation backed by
**OkHttp 5.x** (`com.squareup.okhttp3:okhttp-jvm`). Consider it when:

- You want transparent HTTP/2 with automatic HTTP/1.1 fallback.
- You are developing for Android, where OkHttp is the de-facto HTTP client.
- You want efficient request/response body streaming with minimal in-memory buffering (OkHttp

  application and want to share the same `OkHttpClient` instance.

The transport is auto-discovered via `ServiceLoader` when the module is on the classpath. An
explicit `.transport(...)` call always wins over auto-discovery.

## Maven Dependencies

```xml
<!-- Juneau transport adapter -->
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.apache.juneau</groupId>
    <artifactId>juneau-rest-client-jetty</artifactId>
    <version>${juneau.version}</version>
</dependency>

<!-- Jetty 12 HTTP Client (transitive from the adapter, pinned here for clarity) -->
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.eclipse.jetty</groupId>
    <artifactId>jetty-client</artifactId>
    <version>12.1.9</version>
</dependency>
```

---

## Overview

`juneau-rest-client-jetty` provides an `HttpTransport` implementation backed by the **Jetty 12
`HttpClient`** (`org.eclipse.jetty:jetty-client`). Consider it when:

- Your application already embeds a Jetty server (e.g., via
  [juneau-microservice-jetty](/docs/topics/JuneauMicroserviceJetty)) and you want to share
  the same Jetty lifecycle for outbound HTTP calls.
- You want a Jetty-native HTTP client without pulling in Apache HttpComponents or OkHttp.

The request body is streamed via `OutputStreamRequestContent` on a background thread, so large
bodies do not require full in-memory buffering. Response body bytes are made available as an
`InputStream` via Jetty's `InputStreamResponseListener`.

The transport is auto-discovered via `ServiceLoader` when the module is on the classpath. An
explicit `.transport(...)` call always wins over auto-discovery.

---

## Getting Started

### Zero-configuration default

:::tip Note
`JettyHttpTransport.create()` and `JettyHttpTransportBuilder.build()` declare `throws Exception`
because they may need to start the underlying Jetty `HttpClient`.
:::

```java
import org.apache.juneau.marshall.json5.*;
import org.apache.juneau.rest.client.*;
import org.apache.juneau.rest.client.jetty.*;

RestClient client;
try {
    client = RestClient.builder()
        .transport(JettyHttpTransport.create())   // starts a new HttpClient internally
        .serializer(Json5Serializer.DEFAULT)
        .parser(Json5Parser.DEFAULT)

description:
The NG `RestClient` protects outbound calls against server-side request forgery (SSRF) and credential
leaks across redirects. This page describes what is enforced, where, and how to opt out. The same
URL policy class (`org.apache.juneau.http.remote.RemoteUrlPolicy`, in `juneau-rest-common`) is shared
with the classic client.

:::info Which calls are covered?
The SSRF guard (URL deny-list, pin-on-connect, per-hop redirect re-validation) applies to
**policy-covered** calls: `@Remote` / `@RemoteOp` proxies and dynamic `@Url` arguments, or a request
where you called `remoteUrlPolicy(true, ...)`. An ordinary `client.get("https://...")` is treated as
trusted application code and is not run through the deny-list.
:::

## URL policy

`RemoteUrlPolicy.requireAllowedUrl(url, allowPrivate)` rejects a URL unless:

- the scheme is `http` or `https` and the host is non-empty;
- the host is not on the deny-list: `localhost`, `localhost.localdomain`, `metadata.google.internal`
  (and its subdomains), or an IP literal that is loopback, any-local, link-local, site-local (RFC 1918),
  IPv6 unique-local (`fc00::/7`), IPv4 `0.0.0.0/8` ("this network"), IPv4 `100.64.0.0/10` (carrier-grade NAT
  shared space, which stays denied), IPv4 special-purpose ranges `192.0.0.0/24` (IETF protocol assignments),
  `198.18.0.0/15` (benchmarking), `224.0.0.0/4` (multicast) and `240.0.0.0/4` (reserved, including `255.255.255.255`),
  IPv6 multicast (`ff00::/8`), IPv6 Teredo (`2001::/32`) or IPv6 local-use NAT64 (`64:ff9b:1::/48`). The last two are denied outright, because the
  embedded IPv4 address is obfuscated or its embedding length is operator-defined. IPv6 addresses that embed an IPv4 address
  (IPv4-mapped, IPv4-compatible, IPv4-translated `::ffff:0:a.b.c.d`, NAT64 `64:ff9b::/96`,
  and 6to4 `2002::/16`) are unwrapped and classified by the embedded IPv4 address. IPv6 zone ids
  (`[fe80::1%25en0]`) are ignored for classification, and an unparseable IPv6 literal is denied.

To re-permit a lab or...

description: ## Contents/Features The `juneau-rest-mock` module contains convenience APIs for performing serverless unit testing of your REST APIs. Each of the APIs provides the ability to fully test your server and client REST interfaces without the need for a running servlet container. See the guide: [Test an endpoint with MockRestClient](/docs/guides/TestAnEndpoint) Tests run entirely in-process. The mock client performs full serialization and parsing of the HTTP request and response, then dispatches the request directly to the resource's RestOpInvoker rather than sending it over the wire. This makes tests fast and self-contained while still exercising nearly all of the client- and server-side code paths — the actual over-the-wire transmission is the only aspect being bypassed. The module ships two flavors of mock client: - The classic MockRestClient — built on the Apache HttpClient 4.5–based classic RestClient, exposing its full fluent surface. This is the client documented in [Mock REST Client Overview](/docs/topics/MockRestClientOverview). - The next-generation MockRestClient — paired with the transport-agnostic RestClient, for tests that target the new stack. See [Next-Generation REST Client](/docs/topics/NextGenRestClient) for examples. Both clients live in the same Maven module and can be mixed in a single project. Mock Testing Classes

description:
The `juneau-rest-mock` module provides two ways to test code that uses the NG
[`RestClient`](/docs/topics/NextGenRestClient) without a network:

| Class | Use it to test |
|---|---|
| `org.apache.juneau.rest.mock.MockRestClient` | A `@Rest` resource, in-process. The request is dispatched straight to the resource's `RestContext`. |
| `org.apache.juneau.rest.mock.MockHttpTransport` | *Client* code (a `RestClient` or `@Remote` proxy) against canned responses that you define. |

See the guide: [Test an endpoint with MockRestClient](/docs/guides/TestAnEndpoint)

The classic mock client is documented in [Mock REST Client Overview](/docs/topics/MockRestClientOverview).

## MockRestClient (test a `@Rest` resource)

`MockRestClient` wraps a `RestClient` whose transport calls the resource directly. The argument is a
`@Rest` bean instance or class. Request paths are relative to the resource's `@Rest(path)`, so for a
`PetResource` annotated `@Rest(path="/pets")`, `mock.get("/1")` reaches `/pets/1`. A path of `/pets/1` would
look for `/pets/pets/1` and return a 404.

```java
try (MockRestClient mock = MockRestClient.create(PetResource.class);
        var resp = mock.get("/1").run()) {
    resp.assertThat().isOk().body().contains("Fido");
}
```

The verb methods (`get`, `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`, `head`, `request`) return the same
[`RestRequest`](/docs/topics/NgRequests) as a real client, so [assertions](/docs/topics/NgAssertions),
[interceptors](/docs/topics/NgInterceptors) and typed bodies all work. `getClient()` exposes the
underlying `RestClient`, for example to create a `@Remote` proxy:

```java
PetApi api = mock.getClient().remote(PetApi.class);
```

### Builder

```java
MockRestClient mock = MockRestClient.builder(new PetResource())
    .contextPath("/app")
    .defaultParser(Json5Parser.create().build())
    .build();
```

| Method | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `contextPath(String)` | Simulates a servlet context path. The root URL becomes `http://localhost` + context ...

## Contents/Features

Juneau Microservice is an API for creating stand-alone executable jars with automatic support for Juneau configurations
and console commands.

Features include:

- A builder-based API for defining and starting microservices.
- An extensible API that allows you to hook into various lifecycle events.
- Simple-to-use APIs for accessing manifest file entries, command-line arguments, and external configuration file properties.
- A bean-store-aware inject-style bootstrap (`@Configuration` + `@Bean`) that lets companion modules — such as `juneau-microservice-jetty` — contribute servers, listeners, and servlets through standard `@Bean` definitions, rather than via subclassing.

## When to use it

Use `juneau-microservice` when you want a stand-alone executable jar that reads its settings from a config file and manifest. Add `juneau-microservice-jetty` to serve REST resources.

## Example

```java
import org.apache.juneau.microservice.*;

public class MyMicroservice {

    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        // Build the microservice from the command-line arguments, start it, and wait for it to stop.
        Microservice.create().args(args).build().start().join();
    }
}
```

## Options

| Builder method | Use it to |
|---|---|
| `args(String...)` | Pass the command-line arguments |
| `listener(MicroserviceListener)` | React to start, stop and config changes |

## Module Name (Renamed in 10.0)

In 10.0 this module was renamed from `juneau-microservice-core` to `juneau-microservice`. The Java package
([org.apache.juneau.microservice](pathname:///site/apidocs/org/apache/juneau/microservice/package-summary.html)) is unchanged. See the [V10 Migration Guide](/docs/topics/V10MigrationGuide) for the
exact dependency update.

## See also

- [Microservice Overview](/docs/topics/MicroserviceOverview)
- [Microservice Listeners](/docs/topics/...

description:
Juneau microservices are **self-contained, deployable REST servers** built on top of the Juneau REST
server framework. A microservice packages your REST resources, configuration, and an embedded HTTP container
into a single executable jar (or WAR) that you can start with a plain `java -jar` command.

The microservice layer builds on top of the full Juneau stack:

<tree>
<node-0>Juneau Microservice Stack</node-0>
<node-1>juneau-microservice — core lifecycle, config, console, inject bootstrap</node-1>
<node-1>juneau-rest-server — @Rest / @RestOp REST engine (serialization, routing, guards, …)</node-1>
<node-1>juneau-marshall — multi-format POJO marshalling (JSON, XML, HTML, YAML, …)</node-1>
<node-1>Deployment target (one of Jetty / Tomcat / Spring Boot)</node-1>
</tree>

---

## Deployment Targets

Juneau provides three independently-releasable deployment adapters.  All three share the same
`Microservice` + `@Configuration` + `@Bean Servlet` programming model and the same lifecycle contracts.

| Module | When to use |
|---|---|
| [juneau-microservice-jetty](/docs/topics/JuneauMicroserviceJetty) | Default choice for standalone runnable jars. Ships a zero-config `JettyMicroservice.run(args, servlet)` one-liner and a classpath-driven `jetty.xml` knob for advanced connector tuning. |
| [juneau-microservice-tomcat](/docs/topics/JuneauMicroserviceTomcat) | Drop-in alternative when your organisation standardises on Tomcat, or when you want to share `[Tomcat]` config between an embedded dev launcher and a full Tomcat deployment. |
| [juneau-rest-server-springboot](/docs/topics/JuneauRestServerSpringboot) | Integration point for Spring Boot applications. REST resources extend `BasicSpringRestServlet` / `BasicSpringRestServletGroup` so Spring `@Autowired` injection and `@Bean` resolution flow through the Spring application context instead of the Juneau bean store. |

All three adapters depend on [juneau-microservice](/docs/topics/JuneauMicroservice) for the core
